speaker: will_kemp
text: Flour in your eyebrow, Master Shakespeare. Either the ghost has been baking, or the stable has opinions.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The sheet, and the flour, and the boards over my head. I heard the horses cough. That I will swear to.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: The gallery of lawyers went quiet. I had it from the stage, at the end of the light. Thou wert under the boards, so the quiet is mine to tell and the horses are thine.

speaker: john_sincler
text: Quiet after the cry, or quiet instead of it? I was off in the tiring-house. I heard the line. I did not see the lawyers any better than he did.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: After it. They had been rustling like a term-time ordinary, and the cry took the rustle away. That is what I had from up here. Not a face of his. He was not up here.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then keep the gallery. I am not coming up to collect a face I did not have. The light was going. One line is what the last of it gets.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: It worked, as it does. I am not going to teach a yard to be quiet. The line does that, and thou wert not there to see it done.

speaker: will_kemp
text: You were more fearful a fortnight ago, with the cold. You are not now. I had hoped for a tremble. A man likes his ghosts inexpensive and a little afraid.

speaker: will_kemp
text: A fortnight ago you would have coughed in time with the horses, and called it art. Tonight you are only dusty. I can tell the difference, and I am sorry for the art.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The fortnight was the cold. This is flour. I am not mixing them to give you a better story.

speaker: john_sincler
text: How does a man stand so as to look dead? I am asking it straight. I have to bring a message in black, and I would rather not look as if I had run.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Think of the reckoning, John.

speaker: john_sincler
text: The reckoning. Stand as if the sum were already bad, and the face will follow the feet.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Stand as if you already know the number, and you will not need to pull a dead face on over a live one. You need no padding to look like bad news. John Heminges said so, and the black will do the rest.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Two ghosts today, if a man wants a comparison. Ours under the floor, and across the river a conqueror who dies in his own second part. Thou didst not go, Will. I am glad of the voice.

speaker: will_kemp
text: The second Tamburlaine may keep the Bankside. I have had enough of one ghost. You, Master Shakespeare, may wash before you sit on a bench I mean to use.

speaker: john_sincler
text: I will take the reckoning as a note and not as a joke. If I play it for a laugh, tell me on Thursday, not after the lawyers have gone home.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It was not a joke. Think of the reckoning when you want the body to stop explaining itself. The cry is one line. It does not need a second.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Hamlet, revenge. Thou hast spent it. Do not spend it again in the parlour for our comfort.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Too late. I have heard it through the boards, and I have heard it in a clean shirt, and the second time was the less frightening. You are well. Say so, and sit.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am well. I was more fearful a fortnight ago. I will not make the flour into a boast on the way home.

speaker: john_sincler
text: Then I have what I asked. Bad news, in black, and the feet still. Thank you, Will.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Wash, and go. The Rose has had its ghost. We have had ours. I am not staging a third in this room.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Third ghost is a dinner story, and you have already refused me the tremble. I am going to the ale. You are going to a basin, if you love your landlady.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A basin, and home. The horses coughed. The lawyers, Dick, I leave with thee. I did not see them.
